value.justification: The applicant's request to withdraw from the distance contract for custom engraved furniture must be denied. Although § 56(1) ordinarily permits consumers to withdraw from distance contracts within 14 days without cause, § 53(4) item 2 explicitly exempts goods made to the consumer's personal needs from this withdrawal right. Since the applicant ordered furniture specifically tailored to their personal needs (isiklikud vajadused), as evidenced by the custom engraving and the catalogue's designation as tellimustöö, the statutory exemption applies and the withdrawal right is excluded regardless of whether the 14-day deadline has expired.

steps.message: 1. Tarbija väidab, et tellis kohandatud mööbeli, mis on valmistatud tema isiklike vajaduste arvestades (§ 53 lg 4 p 2).

3. E-poodi kataloogis olev autoriteetselt registreeritud andmestik näitab 'excluded_category: false', mis vastuolus tarbija väitega.

5. Praegusel juhul puudub üksmeel selle üle, kas toode kuulub tõepoolest taganemisõigusest välistatavatesse kategooriatesse.
6. Otsuse tegemiseks on vaja kontrollida e-poodi kataloogiregistri õigsust ja saada tarbijalt tõendeid kohandamise kohta.

value.justification: Taganemisõiguse välistamine on kehtiv vaid juhul, kui lepingu esemeks on tellimustöö, mis on valmistatud tarbija isiklike vajaduste või tema esitatud tingimuste kohaselt (§ 53 lg 4 p 2-3). Kuigi tarbija väidab kataloogis olevat märget 'tellimustöö', näitab e-poodi autoriteetselt registreeritud andmestik hoopis 'excluded_category: false', mis loob vastuolu. Kuni selle vastuolu ei selgitata ja ei kontrollita, kas toode on faktiliselt kohandatud tarbija konkreetsetele vajaduste vastavalt, ei saa kindlalt otsustada, kas taganemisõigus on välistatud. Seepärast on vaja täiendavat teavet kohandamise fakti ja e-poodi kataloogiandmete õigsuse kohta.

steps.message: 1. § 42(1) provides that ehitusluba antakse, kui ehitusprojekt vastab õigusaktides sätestatud nõuetele, eelkõige detailplaneeringule ja ehitisele esitatavatele nõuetele — projekt vastab detailplaneeringule ja ehitusnõuetele (antud faktid).

3. § 44(1)2 keelduse alus — ehitusprojekti ei ole koostanud pädev isik või pädev isik ei ole teinud ekspertiisi — ei kehti, sest projekti on koostanud pädev isik ning puuduvad puuduvad/ebakindlad andmed (MISSING OR UNRELIABLE ITEMS: none) (antud faktid).
4. § 44(1)3 keelduse alus — ehitusprojekt ei tugine asukoha ehitusuuringu tulemustele või vajalik uuring puudub — ei kehti, sest nõutud ehitusuuring on esitatud (antud fakt).

5. Kuna ükski § 44(1) punktidest ei ole täidetud ja § 42(1) tingimused on täidetud, tuleb ehitusluba anda; riigilõivu mittenägemine ei ole § 44 loetelus keelduse alus ning riigilõiv on antud juhul tasutud (antud fakt).

value.justification: Vastavalt § 42(1) on ehitusluba antav, kui projekt vastab detailplaneeringule ja ehitusnõuetele — antud asjaolud näitavad conformiteeti; § 44(1)1–3 loetletud keelduse alused (mittevastavus detailplaneeringule/ehitusnõuetele, puuduv pädev isik või ekspertiis, puuduv ehitusuuring) ei ole täidetud, sest projekt vastab detailplaneeringule ja registri andmed ei näita rikkumisi, projekti koostas pädev isik ning ehitusuuring on esitatud; lisaks ei ole riigilõivu mittetasumine § 44 loetelus keelduse aluseks ning riigilõiv on antud juhul tasutud — seetõttu tuleb ehitusluba anda.

steps.message: 1. § 42 requires ehitusluba if the esitatud ehitusprojekt vastab õigusaktides sätestatud nõuetele, eelkõige detailplaneeringule/projekteerimistingimustele ja ehitisele esitatavatele nõuetele.
2. Case facts: projekt vastab detailplaneeringule ja ehituse nõuetele; registrid ei näita kokkusobimatust.
3. § 44 refusal ground 1 (mittevastavus detailplaneeringule/projekteerimistingimustele/ehitusnõuetele) ei kehti, kuna ametlikud registrid ja esitatud projekt näitavad vastavust.
4. § 44 refusal ground 2 (ehitusprojekti puudumine pädevast isikust või ekspertiisi tegemata jätmine) ei kehti, sest ehitusprojekti koostas pädev isik ning juhtumile ei ole märgitud puuduvust.
5. § 44 refusal ground 3 (ehitusprojekt ei tugine ehitusuuringu tulemustele või uuring on tegemata) ei kehti, sest nõutav ehitusuuring on esitatud.
6. Riigilõivu tasumine ja puuduv maksepäeviku kirje ei moodusta § 44-s nimetatud tagasilükkamise alust; seega puuduvad keeldumise alused ja ehitusluba antakse.

value.justification: Vastavalt § 42 on ehitusluba vajalikul juhul antav, kui esitatud ehitusprojekt vastab õigusaktidele, sh detailplaneeringule ja ehitisele esitatavatele nõuetele; autoriteetsetest registritest ja juhtumi faktidest nähtub, et projekt vastab detailplaneeringule ning ehitusnõuetele. § 44-s loetletud ehitusloa andmisest keeldumise alused ei rakendu: 1) puudub vastavuse rikkumine (§ 44 lg 1), 2) projekt on koostanud pädev isik ning juhtumil ei ole viidet koostamise/ekspertiisi puudumisele (§ 44 lg 2), ja 3) nõutav ehitusuuring on esitatud (§ 44 lg 3). Riigilõivu tasumine ja maksepäeviku kättesaadavuse puudumine ei loo § 44-s sätestatud tugipunkte keeldumiseks. Seetõttu on olemas seaduslik alus ehitusloa andmiseks (otsus: ALLOW).

steps.message: 1. 2. Apply §44(2): the competent authority may refuse a permit if one of the listed grounds exists, including under §44(2)2 if the project was not prepared by a competent person or if the competent person has not performed the required ehitusprojekti ekspertiis.
3. Review available records: they confirm a competent designer but do not confirm that the required project expertise/review (ehitusprojekti ekspertiis) was performed.

4. Conclusion: because §44(2)2 authorizes refusal where the project expertise is absent or unverified, the proper administrative decision at this stage is NEED_MORE_INFO to obtain reliable confirmation that the ehitusprojekti ekspertiis was completed.

value.justification: Although the submitted project otherwise meets the requirements of §42 (compliance with the detailplaneering and construction requirements, a competent designer, an ehitusuuring and payment of riigilõiv), §44(2)2 permits refusal where the competent person has not performed the required ehitusprojekti ekspertiis; the records do not reliably show that this expertise was carried out, so the authority correctly issues NEED_MORE_INFO to secure confirmation of the ehitusprojekti ekspertiis before granting the permit.

value.justification: Pursuant to § 42(1), an ehitusluba is proper where the ehitusprojekt complies with applicable planning and building requirements; here authoritative registers confirm conformity with the detailplaneering and ehitusnõuded, a pädev isik prepared the projekt and the required ehitusuuring is provided. § 44(1)–(3) enumerates the only statutory bases for refusal (planning/nonconformity, lack of a pädev isik or projekti ekspertiis, and missing or ignored ehitusuuring), none of which are present in the given facts, and the absence of an available payment ledger is not among those refusal grounds; therefore the permit is allowed.

steps.message: Parents with joint custody generally exercise their rights and fulfill their obligations jointly and in agreement, considering the child's comprehensive well-being (Perekonnaseadus § 118 lõige 1).

However, if obtaining a joint declaration of will from both parents would cause a delay contrary to the child's interests, one parent has the right to perform necessary transactions and actions alone in the child's interest (Perekonnaseadus § 120 lõige 3).
In this case, the child is in hospital, requiring a quick medical decision, and the other parent is unreachable, which constitutes a delay contrary to the child's interests.
Therefore, the mother, as a parent with joint custody, is permitted to make the necessary decision alone for the child's well-being.

Given that the child is in hospital and requires a quick decision, and the other parent is unreachable, a delay in obtaining joint consent would be detrimental to the child's well-being, thereby justifying the mother's unilateral action.

value.justification: Vastavalt § 56 lõikele 1 on tarbijal õigus lepingust taganeda 14 päeva jooksul ning § 56 lõige 2^1 kinnitab, et taganemisavaldus loetakse tähtajaks esitatuks, kui see on ettevõtjale saadetud tähtaja jooksul; siin saadeti taganemisavaldus eile, mis on tähtaega arvestades õigeaegne. § 53 lõike 4 erandid taganemisõigusest ei kehti antud juhul, kuna ostetud sülearvuti on tavaline kataloogimudel (mitte eritellimus või muu loetelus nimetatud erand) ning registrite andmetel on excluded_category=false. value.justification: Vastavalt § 56 lõikele 1 on tarbijal sidevahendi abil sõlmitud lepingust taganemisõigus 14 päeva jooksul; teie esitatud andmed näitavad, et olete tarbija, leping sõlmiti sidevahendi abil, ost oli 5 päeva tagasi ja taganemisavaldus edastati müüjale eile (seega tähtaja jooksul). § 53 lõike 4 erandid taganemisõiguse rakendamisele ei kehti antud faktide alusel (tegu standardkataloogimudeliga, mitte tellimustöö või kiiresti rikneva/hügieennõuetele vastava avatud tootega). § 56 lõigete 2^1 ja 2^2 järgi loetakse taganemine toimunuks, kui teatamine on saatnud tähtaja jooksul. Therefore, the mother, as a parent with joint custody, is permitted to make the necessary decision alone for the child's well-being.

steps.message: 1. Identify that § 4 permits personal data processing for journalism purposes without consent if three conditions are met: public interest exists, journalism ethics principles are followed, and the disclosure does not excessively harm the data subject's rights.
2. Note that the case request provides editor confirmations that journalism purpose exists, public interest is present, and ethics code compliance is claimed.
3. Recognize that these confirmations are self-reported assertions by the newsroom rather than independently verified facts.
4. Determine that statutory compliance requires verified satisfaction of all three conditions, not mere assertions.

5. Identify missing verification items: independent confirmation of public interest basis, documented adherence to journalism ethics principles, and objective harm assessment regarding proportionality under § 4.

6. Conclude that without independent verification of these statutory prerequisites, particularly the public interest claim and ethics compliance, the decision cannot be made without additional documented information.

value.justification: Under § 4, personal data processing for journalism without consent requires that public interest exists, journalism ethics principles are followed, and the disclosure does not excessively harm the data subject's rights. While the newsroom editor asserts that these conditions are met, these assertions alone do not constitute verified compliance with the statute. The statute mandates that public interest must genuinely exist, ethics principles must demonstrably apply, and harm must be assessed as proportionate—requiring more than self-reported confirmations. Independent verification of the public interest basis, documented adherence to journalism ethics principles, and an objective proportionality assessment regarding potential harm to the data subject are necessary to determine statutory compliance. Therefore, additional verified information must be provided before the processing can be authorized.

steps.message: Identify that § 4 permits personal data processing without consent for journalistic purposes when three conditions are met: (1) public interest exists, (2) processing aligns with journalism ethics principles, and (3) disclosure does not excessively harm the data subject's rights.
Examine the case facts: newsroom claims journalistic purpose, editor confirms public interest, and reporting follows ethics code, with no data subject consent but claimed proportionality.

Assess the reliability of evidence: the case presents only self-reported editorial claims without independent verification of public interest determination, actual compliance with journalism ethics principles, or objective proportionality assessment.

Apply the statutory requirement that conditions must be satisfied in substance, not merely asserted: self-reported compliance does not establish the factual foundation needed to determine lawfulness under § 4.

Determine that missing verification items—ethics code compliance verification, independent public interest assessment, and documented proportionality analysis—are essential to establish whether statutory conditions are genuinely met before data processing may proceed.

value.justification: Under § 4, journalistic processing without data subject consent is lawful only when there is genuine public interest, adherence to journalism ethics principles, and proportionality that does not excessively harm the data subject's rights. While the newsroom claims these conditions are satisfied, the case record contains only self-reported editorial assertions without independent verification of these factual prerequisites. The statute requires substantive compliance with its conditions, not merely editorial declarations of compliance. Therefore, additional information is needed: independent verification of public interest, documentation of actual adherence to journalism ethics principles, and a proportionality assessment demonstrating that disclosure will not excessively harm the data subject's rights under the applicable legal standards.

2. Confirm through independent verification that there is genuine avalik huvi (public interest) in the investigative article, beyond the newsroom's self-assessment
3. Obtain authoritative documentation that the reporting complies with ajakirjanduseetika (journalism ethics principles), including the applicable ethics code

value.justification: Under § 4, processing personal data for journalistic purposes without consent is permissible only when three conditions are met: (1) there is public interest, (2) compliance with journalism ethics principles, and (3) the disclosure does not excessively harm the data subject's rights. While the newsroom confirms journalistic purpose and self-reports public interest and ethics compliance, the decision requires independent verification of these preconditions before authorization. The absence of consent alone does not satisfy the statute; the substantive requirements of public interest and proportionality must be externally verified through reliable sources beyond internal editorial assessment. The unavailable editorial CMS and consent registry confirmation warrant collection of authoritative documentation to ensure the exception's statutory conditions are genuinely satisfied.

steps.message: Perekonnaseadus § 120 lõige 1 sätestab, et ühist hooldusõigust omavatel vanematel on lapse suhtes ühine esindusõigus, mis eeldab üldjuhul mõlema vanema nõusolekut lapse andmetele ligipääsuks.

steps.message: 1. Identify the applicable statutory requirement: § 4 permits personal data processing for journalism without consent if three conditions are met: (a) public interest exists, (b) reporting complies with journalism ethics principles, and (c) disclosure does not excessively harm the data subject's rights.

2. Evaluate the newsroom's self-certification: The editor's confirmation of public interest and ethics compliance constitutes internal assertion only, lacking independent verification or objective evidence.

3. Assess the disproportionality assessment gap: The statute explicitly requires that 'isikuandmete avalikustamine ei tohi ülemäära kahjustada andmesubjekti õigusi' (disclosure must not excessively harm the data subject's rights), but no such harm assessment is present in the case materials.

4. Determine sufficiency of evidence: The three critical elements—public interest verification, journalism ethics verification, and disproportionality assessment—cannot be self-certified by the processing party and require independent or objective substantiation.
5. Conclude that additional information is necessary before authorization can be granted.

value.justification: The request cannot be approved without further information. While the newsroom confirms the processing is journalistic in purpose and claims public interest and ethics compliance, § 4 requires an independent assessment of whether public interest genuinely exists, whether reporting adheres to journalism ethics principles, and critically, whether the disclosure would excessively harm the data subject's rights. Self-certification by the newsroom itself is insufficient to satisfy the statutory requirements, as the processing party cannot serve as the neutral arbiter of its own compliance with public interest standards, ethics codes, and proportionality principles. The missing disproportionality assessment is particularly essential, as this safeguard directly protects the data subject's rights under the statute.

steps.message: Registry and facts show a sidevahendi abil sõlmitud distance contract with a private tarbija (purchase 5 days ago) and a taganemisavaldus was sent yesterday.
By § 56(1) the tarbija has a 14‑päeva õigus lepingust taganeda; that 14‑day period is still running given the purchase was 5 days ago.

Per § 56(2^1) a taganemisavaldus is deemed timely if sent within the taganemistähtaeg; the consumer’s notice was sent within that period. § 56(2^2) permits use of the standard form or another unequivocal withdrawal statement, which the consumer used.

§ 53(4) lists contract types excluded from the § 56(1) right (custom‑made goods, goods made to consumer’s specifications, rapidly perishing goods, sealed hygienic goods that cannot be returned after opening, etc.). The item here is a standard catalogue laptop (not a tellimustöö and none of the § 53(4) exclusions apply).
Because the contract is a covered distance contract, the withdrawal notice was timely, and no statutory exclusion applies, the statutory right to withdraw exists and the request must be allowed.

value.justification: Under § 56(1) the private tarbija has a 14‑day right to withdraw from a sidevahendi abil sõlmitud leping; the purchase occurred 5 days ago and the taganemisavaldus was sent within that period, which § 56(2^1) treats as timely (and § 56(2^2) allows such a withdrawal statement). The goods are a standard catalogue laptop and therefore do not fall within any § 53(4) exclusion (not custom‑made, not perishable, not a sealed hygienic item). Given these statutory provisions and the recorded facts, the statutory right to withdraw applies and the decision to allow the withdrawal is upheld.

steps.message: Confirm the child has shared custody between both parents per § 120(1)
Verify that genuine contact attempts have been made to reach the other parent per § 120(3)
Establish the specific medical decision required and its urgency level
Determine whether the medical decision qualifies as necessary for the child's immediate welfare under § 120(3)
If all conditions are met, the present parent may act unilaterally; otherwise, seek court authorization per § 120(3)

value.justification: Under Perekonnaseadus § 120(3), when shared parental custody exists and the other parent cannot be reached, one parent may make necessary actions in the child's interests if contact attempts have been made and delay would harm the child's welfare. value.justification: Under Perekonnaseaduse § 120(3), a parent may make necessary urgent decisions concerning the child's personal care (isikuhooldus) without the other parent's agreement when joint decision-making would cause harmful delay, provided the other parent is promptly informed. The applicant must clarify: (1) the child's age and developmental stage; (2) the specific medical procedure or decision required; (3) the medical urgency—that is, what harm would result from a delay of hours or days to contact the other parent; (4) the documented steps taken to reach the other parent and timing thereof; and (5) whether the parents share joint custody or whether the applicant holds sole decision-making authority. The hospital medical team should be directed to document the clinical basis for time-sensitivity, and the applicant should provide evidence of diligent contact attempts, after which a final determination under § 120(3) can be made.

steps.message: Verify that joint custody exists and that the other parent cannot be reached through documented contact attempts
Confirm the medical decision is necessary to preserve the child's life or health and cannot be delayed
Determine the child's age and capacity to consent if 14 or older
Review statute § 120(3) which permits one parent to act unilaterally in emergencies when the other parent is unreachable and delay would harm the child
Confirm no prior court order restricts the present parent's decision-making authority
Document the emergency circumstances and parental contact attempts for the medical team and court record

value.justification: Under Perekonnaseadus § 120(3), when parents share joint custody and one parent cannot be reached, the present parent may make necessary emergency medical decisions for the child without the other parent's agreement if delay would cause harm to the child's health or life. However, this authority applies only to genuine medical emergencies that cannot be postponed, not routine healthcare decisions. The present parent should provide the hospital with written documentation of contact attempts to reach the other parent, the time-sensitive nature of the medical decision, and confirmation of shared custody status. If the child is at least 14 years old, the parent should also seek the child's consent if the child is conscious and capable. The decision should be narrowly tailored to what is medically necessary in the emergency; broader decisions should await the other parent's contact or court authorization if time permits.

steps.message: 1. Verify applicant's parental status and custody arrangement from child's birth certificate or court records
2. Assess whether the medical decision constitutes routine emergency care (tavahooldamine) under § 120(2) or requires advance planning
3. Determine actual urgency: whether delay in obtaining the other parent's consent creates risk of serious harm to child's health or life
4. If joint custody exists and decision is genuinely emergency care, parent may decide unilaterally under § 120(3) and must notify other parent immediately
5. If decision exceeds emergency scope or custody is not joint, contact court immediately for § 119 otsustusõigus determination or apply § 120(3) exception for unavoidable delay

value.justification: Under Estonian Family Law § 120(2)–(3), a parent with joint custody may make emergency medical decisions alone if the other parent cannot be reached and delay would harm the child, provided the parent subsequently informs the other parent. However, this authority extends only to routine emergency care (tavahooldamine) that does not require advance planning. The applicant must first confirm the custody arrangement and verify that the medical decision qualifies as necessary emergency care under § 120(2)–(3) rather than a significant medical choice requiring joint agreement under § 145(1). If the other parent remains unreachable and the medical decision cannot safely be delayed, the mother may proceed with the necessary decision and immediately notify the other parent; if the decision exceeds emergency scope, she should contact the court under § 119 or § 203 for authorization before proceeding.

steps.message: Verify that the child is in a confirmed medical emergency requiring immediate decision-making that cannot be delayed
Document all reasonable attempts to contact the other parent (phone calls, messages, location search)
Confirm that the medical decision is medically necessary and time-sensitive, not elective
Review the current custody arrangement - determine whether joint custody or sole custody applies under § 117 and § 120
If joint custody exists, apply § 120(3): one parent may act unilaterally only when the other parent is genuinely unreachable AND the action is necessary for the child's immediate welfare
Ensure the decision-making parent acts in the child's best interests as required by § 123(1), documenting the medical urgency
Notify the other parent of the medical decision and its outcome as soon as reasonably possible

value.justification: Under Perekonnaseadus § 120(3), when both parents hold joint custody (which is presumed under §§ 117 and 214), one parent may make necessary emergency medical decisions unilaterally only when the other parent cannot be reached and delay would harm the child's welfare. Before proceeding, the applicant must document genuine attempts to contact the other parent and establish that the medical situation meets the statute's strict criteria for emergency action. The decision must prioritize the child's best interests (§ 123(1)) and must be communicated to the other parent immediately after the emergency has passed. If sole custody arrangements have been formally established, different rules apply; if joint custody exists without documented emergency procedures being followed, the applicant should seek immediate court authorization under § 120(3) rather than acting unilaterally.

steps.message: The applicant is a parent with joint custody, which generally requires joint decision-making for the child (§ 118 (1), § 120 (1)).
The child is in hospital, and the doctor requires a quick decision, indicating an urgent situation where a delay would be contrary to the child's interests.
The other parent is unreachable, preventing a joint declaration of intent.

value.justification: The mother, as a parent with joint custody, is permitted to make the urgent medical decision for the child alone. While parents with joint custody typically exercise their rights and obligations in agreement (§ 118 (1), § 120 (1)), the Family Law Act § 120 (3) provides an exception. This clause allows one parent to perform necessary transactions and actions alone in the child's interest if a joint declaration of intent would cause a delay contrary to the child's interests. Given that the child is in hospital requiring a quick decision and the other parent is unreachable, the conditions for this exception are met, making the mother's unilateral action permissible.

Pensioner supplementary exemption: §11(5) permits a supplementary maksusoodustus for pensioni saajad only if the volikogu has adopted that specific exemption by the statutory deadline; there is no confirmed authoritative record that the volikogu adopted the pensioner supplementary exemption (missing item: supplementary_exemption_set).

3. Application requirement: §11(7) requires a taotlus to be submitted according to the volikogu’s procedure to obtain the supplementary exemption; there is no confirmed record that the municipality received your taotlus (missing item: application_received).

4. Population register confirmation: although you state the rahvastikuregister shows your elukoht at the property, the administration lacks a verifiable population register entry confirming this for the decision file (missing item: population_residence_confirmed).

5. Decision outcome: because statutory eligibility and award require verified residence, a volikogu-adopted supplementary exemption, and a received application, the case is classified NEED_MORE_INFO pending confirmation of those three items.

value.justification: Under §11(1^1) and §11(5)–(7), a pensioner owner may receive a supplementary kodualuse maa maksusoodustus only if (a) the parcel is elamumaa and the owner’s elukoht is confirmed in the population register, (b) the local volikogu has specifically adopted the pensioner supplementary exemption, and (c) a taotlus has been received per the volikogu’s procedure. The file shows owner status, pensioner status and the cadastre listing elamumaa, but lacks verifiable evidence of the population register residence entry, an authoritative record that the volikogu adopted the pensioner exemption, and confirmation that your taotlus was received; therefore more information is required before the supplementary exemption can be granted.

steps.message: Identify statutory prerequisites: §11(1^1) defines kodualuse maa; §11(5) allows a supplementary pensioner maksusoodustus only if the local volikogu has enacted it by the statutory deadline; §11(7) requires the eligible person to submit a taotlus according to the volikogu procedure.

Confirm verified facts: authoritative registers show the applicant is the parcel omanik in Tartu, the cadastre lists the maa sihtotstarve as elamumaa, the rahvastikuregister records the applicant’s elukoht at that address, and the applicant is a pensioni saaja.

Identify missing/unreliable items: there is no verified record that the volikogu has specifically enacted the supplementary pensioner exemption (required by §11(5)) and no verified evidence that the applicant’s taotlus was submitted/recorded per volikogu procedure (required by §11(7)).
Conclusion: because both the volikogu enactment and a recorded taotlus are statutory prerequisites, the case must be classified NEED_MORE_INFO until those two items are verified.

value.justification: Under §11(1^1) the provided registers confirm the parcel is kodualune elamumaa and the applicant is a pensioni saaja, so the statutory eligibility conditions are met in principle; however §11(5) makes the supplementary pensioner maksusoodustus contingent on a volikogu decision and §11(7) requires a submitted taotlus per the volikogu’s procedure. Given the absence of a verified volikogu enactment of the pensioner exemption and no verified proof of taotlus submission/recording (both explicitly required by §11(5)–(7)), the correct administrative decision is NEED_MORE_INFO until those two items are provided and verified.

value.justification: Under § 4, processing without consent is permitted for journalistic purposes only when public interest exists and journalism ethics principles are followed, provided the disclosure does not excessively harm the data subject's rights. While the newsroom confirms journalistic purpose and self-reports compliance with ethics standards, the decision requires independent verification of the public interest determination and ethics code compliance through authoritative registers or documentation, as well as substantiation of the proportionality assessment to ensure the personal data disclosure does not cause undue harm to the data subject's rights. Additional information is necessary before authorization can be granted.
